readings.title: Hezekiah Seeks Counsel from Isaiah
readings.subtitle: The king mourns and sends emissaries to the prophet.
readings.text: [2 Kings 19:1] And it came to be, when Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu heard it, that he tore his garments, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, [2] and sent <dn>את</dn> Elyaqim, who was over the household, and <dn>את</dn> Sheḇnah the scribe, and <dn>את</dn> the elders of the priests, covering themselves with sackcloth, to Yeshayahu the prophet, son of Amots. [3] And they said to him, “Thus said Ḥizqiyahu, ‘This day is a day of distress and rebuke and scorn, for the children have come to birth but there is no power to bring forth. [4] It could be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> does hear <dn>את</dn> all the words of the Raḇshaqěh, whom his master the sovereign of Ashshur has sent to reproach the living <dn>Elohim</dn>, and shall rebuke <dn>את</dn> the words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’ ” [5] And the servants of Sovereign Ḥizqiyahu came to Yeshayahu, [6] and Yeshayahu said to them, “Say this to your master, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Do not be afraid of the words which you have heard, with which the servants of the sovereign of Ashshur have reviled <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am putting a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a report and return to his own land. And <dn>I</dn> shall cause him to fall by the sword in his land.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Sennacherib's Threatening Letter
readings.subtitle: Hezekiah spreads the letter before YeHoVaH and prays for deliverance.
readings.text: [2 Kings 19:8] And the Raḇshaqěh returned and found the sovereign of Ashshur fighting against Liḇnah, for he had heard that he had left Laḵish. [9] And when the sovereign heard concerning Tirhaqah sovereign of Kush, “See, he has come out to fight against you,” he again sent messengers to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, [10] “Speak to Ḥizqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, ‘Do not let your <dn>Elohim</dn> in whom you trust deceive you, saying, “Yerushalayim is not given into the hand of the sovereign of Ashshur.” [11] See, you have heard what the sovereigns of Ashshur have done to all lands by putting them under the ban. And are you going to be delivered? [12] Have the mighty ones of the nations delivered those whom my fathers have destroyed: Gozan and Ḥaran and Retseph, and the sons of Ěḏen who were in Telassar? [13] Where is the sovereign of Ḥamath, and the sovereign of Arpaḏ, and the sovereign of the city of Sepharvayim, Hěna, and Ivvah?’ ” [14] And Ḥizqiyahu received <dn>את</dn> the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them, and went up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Ḥizqiyahu spread it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] And Ḥizqiyahu prayed before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, the One who dwells between the keruḇim, <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone, of all the reigns of the earth. <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> earth. [16] “Incline <dn>Your</dn> ear, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and hear. Open <dn>Your</dn> eyes, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and see. And hear <dn>את</dn> the words of Sanḥěriḇ, which he has sent to reproach the living <dn>Elohim</dn>. [17] “Truly, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the sovereigns of Ashshur have laid waste <dn>את</dn> the nations and their lands, [18] and have put their mighty ones into the fire, for they were not mighty ones, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, and destroyed them. [19] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>I</dn> pray, save us from his hand, so that all the reigns of the earth know that <dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>You</dn> alone.”

readings.title: Hezekiah's Appeal to Isaiah
readings.subtitle: A parallel account of the king's distress and the prophet's initial response.

readings.title: The Letter and the Prayer
readings.subtitle: Hezekiah receives Sennacherib's blasphemous letter and presents it to YeHoVaH.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Rebuke to Sennacherib
readings.subtitle: Through Isaiah, YeHoVaH mocks the Assyrian king's arrogance.
readings.text: [2 Kings 19:20] Then Yeshayahu son of Amots sent to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have heard that which you have prayed to <dn>Me</dn> against Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur.’</dq> [21] <dq>“This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken concerning him, ‘The maiden, the daughter of Tsiyon, has despised you, mocked you; the daughter of Yerushalayim has shaken her head behind you!</dq> [22] <dq>Whom have you reproached and reviled? Against whom have you raised a voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl!</dq> [23] <dq>By the hand of your messengers you have reproached <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “With my many chariots <dn>I</dn> have come up to the height of the mountains, to the sides of Leḇanon. And <dn>I</dn> cut down its tall cedars, its choice cypress trees. And <dn>I</dn> enter its remotest parts, its thickest forest.</dq> [24] <dq><dn>I</dn> have dug and drunk strange water, and with the soles of my feet <dn>I</dn> dry up all the streams of defence.”</dq> [25] <dq>Have you not heard long ago, <dn>I</dn> made it; from days of old <dn>I</dn> formed it? Now <dn>I</dn> have brought it to be, that you should make walled cities ruinous heaps.</dq> [26] <dq>And their inhabitants were powerless, they were overthrown and put to shame, they were as the grass of the field and the green plants, as the grass on the house-tops and withered before it came up.</dq> [27] <dq>But <dn>I</dn> know your sitting down, and your going out and your coming in, and your rage against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>Because your rage against <dn>Me</dn> and your pride have come up to <dn>My</dn> ears, <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>My</dn> hook in your nose and <dn>My</dn> bridle in your lips, and <dn>I</dn> shall turn you back by the way which you came.</dq>

readings.title: The Sign and the Slaughter
readings.subtitle: A remnant will be saved, the Assyrian army is destroyed, and Sennacherib is assassinated.
readings.text: [2 Kings 19:29] <dq>And this is the sign for you: This year you eat what grows of itself, and in the second year what springs from that, and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.</dq> [30] <dq>And the remnant who have escaped of the house of Yehuḏah shall again take root downward, and be fruitful.</dq> [31] <dq>For out of Yerushalayim comes forth a remnant, and those who escape from Mount Tsiyon – the ardour of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does this.’</dq> [32] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘<dn>He</dn> does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.</dq> [33] <dq>By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And he does not come into this city,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [34] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall defend this city, to save it for <dn>My</dn> own sake and for the sake of Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant.’ ”</dq> [35] And it came to be in that night that the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went out, and struck in the camp of Ashshur one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they rose up early in the morning and saw all of them dead bodies. [36] And Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur broke camp and went away, and turned back, and remained in Ninevěh. [37] And it came to be, as he was bowing himself in the house of Nisroḵ his mighty one, that his sons Aḏrammeleḵ and Shar‘etser struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And his son Ěsarḥaddon reigned in his place.

readings.title: The Prophecy Against Sennacherib
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH declares judgment on the Assyrian king for his blasphemous pride.
readings.text: [Isaiah 37:21] Then Yeshayahu son of Amots sent to Ḥizqiyahu, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Because you have prayed to <dn>Me</dn> against Sanḥěriḇ sovereign of Ashshur,</dq> [22] <dq>this is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken concerning him, “The maiden, the daughter of Tsiyon, has despised you, mocked you; the daughter of Yerushalayim has shaken her head behind you!</dq> [23] <dq>“Whom have you reproached and reviled? And against whom have you raised your voice, and lifted up your eyes in pride? Against the Set-apart One of Yisra’ěl!</dq> [24] <dq>“By the hand of your servants you have reproached <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, ‘With my many chariots <dn>I</dn> have come up to the height of the mountains, to the limits of Leḇanon. And <dn>I</dn> cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees. And <dn>I</dn> enter its farthest height, its thickest forest.</dq> [25] <dq><dn>I</dn> have dug and drunk water, and with the soles of my feet <dn>I</dn> have dried up all the streams of defence.’</dq> [26] <dq>“Have you not heard long ago how <dn>I</dn> made it, from days of old, that <dn>I</dn> formed it? Now <dn>I</dn> have brought it about, that you should be for crushing walled cities into heaps of ruins.</dq> [27] <dq>“And their inhabitants were powerless, they were overthrown and put to shame. They were as the grass of the field and as the green plant, as the grass on the house-tops and as grain blighted before it is grown.</dq> [28] <dq>“But <dn>I</dn> know your sitting down, and your going out and your coming in, and your rage against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [29] <dq>“Because your rage against <dn>Me</dn> and your pride have come up to <dn>My</dn> ears, <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>My</dn> hook in your nose and <dn>My</dn> bridle in your lips, and <dn>I</dn> shall turn you back by the way which you came.</dq>

readings.title: The Sign, the Promise, and the Execution
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH gives a sign of restoration and fulfills His word by destroying the Assyrian threat.
readings.text: [Isaiah 37:30] <dq>“And this shall be the sign for you: This year you eat such as grows of itself, and the second year what springs from that, and in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.</dq> [31] <dq>“And the remnant who have escaped of the house of Yehuḏah shall again take root downward, and be fruitful upward.</dq> [32] <dq>“For out of Yerushalayim comes forth a remnant, and those who escape from Mount Tsiyon – the ardour of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts does this.</dq> [33] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning the sovereign of Ashshur, ‘<dn>He</dn> does not come into this city, nor does he shoot an arrow there, nor does he come before it with shield, nor does he build a siege mound against it.</dq> [34] <dq>By the way that he came, by the same he turns back. And into this city he does not come,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [35] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall defend this city, to save it for <dn>My</dn> own sake and for the sake of <dn>My</dn> servant Daviḏ.’ ”</dq> [36] And a messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went out, and struck in the camp of Ashshur one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And they arose early in the morning, and saw all of them, dead bodies. [37] And Sanḥěriḇ the sovereign of Ashshur broke camp and went away, and turned back, and remained at Ninevěh. [38] And it came to be, as he was bowing himself in the house of Nisroḵ his mighty one, that his sons Aḏrammeleḵ and Shar’etser struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat. And his son Ěsarḥaddon reigned in his place.
